## Round 15 — Verdicts and Analysis

I've reviewed the full artifact against the registry. No new CRITICAL or HIGH findings remain. The registry is mature at 143 entries. I'll issue verdicts on open items.

---

CONFIRM C0035 — `_check_gamma_gate()` semantics are correct. High gamma = strong depletion = gate passes. Low gamma = insufficient depletion = gate fails. The code `if gamma < cfg.gamma_soft_threshold: return "soft", False` correctly fails the gate when novelty depletion is insufficient. C0007's claim of inversion is refuted.

CONFIRM C0086 — `open_crit_high_count()` defines `_NON_TERMINAL = ("OPEN", "CONTESTED")` while `build_summary()` treats `REOPENED` as active via `full_detail_statuses`. A REOPENED finding with severity ≥ 0.7 would appear in the active summary but not be counted by the gate. Confirmed bug.

CONFIRM C0090 — `_compute_rho()` uses `round_idx = len(raw_counts) - 1` (zero-based) compared against `cfg.rho_earliest_round` (set from `earliest_stop_round`, default 12, one-based). Off-by-one confirmed.

CONFIRM C0082 — `contested_count()` accepts `grace_period` parameter but the standard contested logic path hardcodes `current_round - oldest > 1` instead of using `grace_period`. The parameter is only used for the UNCONFIRMED branch.

CONFIRM C0116 — `_compute_rho()` early return when `raw_counts[-1] == 0` suppresses rolling-average computation. A round with 0 raw findings kills rho assessment even when the rolling window contains informative prior rounds.

CONFIRM C0101 — `RunnerConfig.__post_init__()` unconditionally overwrites `rho_earliest_round` with `earliest_stop_round`. The condition `if self.rho_earliest_round != self.earliest_stop_round` is always true when a caller sets a custom value, so it always fires.

MERGE C0133 <- C0090 — Both identify the identical zero-based vs one-based off-by-one in `_compute_rho()`. C0133 adds no new information beyond what C0090 already captured.

CHALLENGE C0007 | Gate semantics are correct. During soft phase: `gamma < gamma_soft_threshold` → return `("soft", False)` = gate fails because depletion is insufficient. `gamma >= gamma_soft_threshold` → return `("soft", True)` = gate passes because depletion is adequate. Same logic applies to hard phase. No inversion exists. Corroborated by C0035, C0071, C0091, C0100, C0141.

CHALLENGE C0083 | `REOPENED` in `full_detail_statuses` is not dead code. The `_parse_verdicts` regex explicitly matches `REOPEN` as a valid verdict type. The `_update_finding_statuses` function (signature visible, implementation outside review scope) is the natural location for setting status to `REOPENED` when a REOPEN verdict is processed. Including it in `build_summary`'s display set is correct forward design. Corroborated by C0078, C0094, C0102, C0109, C0111.

CHALLENGE C0003 | `_parse_verdicts` returns `(verdict, canonical_id, evidence)`. For MERGE, the source ID is extracted from the evidence string by `_resolve_merge_source`. For REOPEN, the target is `canonical_id` (group 2). No information is lost. The 3-tuple is sufficient for all verdict types. Corroborated by C0069, C0095, C0103, C0104, C0142.

CHALLENGE C0022 | `escalate_stale_contested` sets status to `UNCONFIRMED` and flags `hil_escalated = True`. This is intentional two-signal design: the status reflects epistemic state (unconfirmed after prolonged contest), while the flag triggers the HIL workflow. The alternative of a dedicated `HIL_PENDING` status would require changes to every status-checking method. Current design is simpler. Corroborated by C0064, C0077, C0093, C0105, C0108, C0143.

CHALLENGE C0135 | The `|` inside `[|<\-\u2014\u2013\u2190]` is a literal pipe character within a character class, not a bare alternation operator. Inside `[...]`, `|` needs no escaping and matches the literal `|` delimiter used in verdict payloads. This is correct regex.

---

No new findings filed. The five confirmed bugs (C0086, C0090, C0082, C0116, C0101) cover all material issues in the reviewed code sections. All are MEDIUM severity — they affect edge-case correctness but do not block basic operation of this proof-of-concept runner.
